The paper presents a new strategy for simultaneous acoustic and electromagnetic invisibility.
The strategy combines four conventional cloaking methods to create a double-cloaking structure.
The double-cloaking structure can hide objects from both acoustic and electromagnetic waves.
The blind mode of cloaking has no acoustic interaction with the outside.
The deaf mode of cloaking has an acoustic link turned on while there is no electromagnetic connection.
The anti-image region in the complementary structure cancels out the acoustic waves.
The Jacobian transformation matrix is used to transform the coordinates of the object and the cloaking structure.
The Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) method is used to simulate Maxwell's equations.
The dispersive FDTD method is a modified version of the FDTD method that can correctly produce the materials applied in the invisible structures.
The EMOSC and PAC structures are used to create a deaf mode of cloaking.
The results shown in Figures 9 and 10 demonstrate the effectiveness of the blind mode of cloaking.
The double-cloaking structure can be used to create invisible objects that can be used in various fields.
The paper presents a new approach to cloaking that can be generalized to any method of cloaking.
The strategy can be used to create dual cloaking such as electromagnetic-elastic, sound-wave, and so on.
